co_low_angle_wall.blurb: Low Angle Wall is the most visited sector of a small roadside crag north of Durango, set among trees at the foot of the cliff. It holds 17 bolted sport routes, with a handful of easy leads around 5.6 to 5.8, a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10, and a couple of 5.11s. The moderate lines make it a comfortable place for newer leaders to build mileage. Mornings are sunny and the afternoon brings shade, so summer days stay tolerable. Holds can be slick and grimy after rain or spring runoff, and some lines are still being cleaned, so fall tends to be the best season.

co_pass_the.blurb: The Pass is a tucked-away boulder cluster on the east side of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park, in the foothills between Morrison and Evergreen. You reach it by following the Sisters trail and climbing east through a narrow gap, and it feels private compared with the busier boulders nearby. Seventeen problems are recorded, mostly V1 to V5 with a few steps above that and two at V8. Many lines are short but the stone is good, and the slopes face east with a mix of sun and shade. It is harder to find than the park's famous blocks.

co_energy_crag.blurb: Energy Crag is a short band of rock on the east side of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park, above Evergreen. It offers more peace than the nearby Egg boulders but takes some effort to locate, with a brief off-trail scramble up a ravine beside a big slab. Of the 17 problems, most run from V0 to V5, and a handful of harder lines reach V6 through V8, with one trad line as well. Expect compact faces with a steady supply of good moves, in a pine forest setting where the park's trails are busy even if this corner is not.

co_diamond_head.blurb: Diamond Head is a remote summit above Eldorado Canyon near Boulder, at the end of a chain of crags that is far less visited than the canyon's main walls. The hike in is long, which keeps the crowds away. Of its 17 climbs, most are traditional routes from easy fifth class to the low 5.12s, with a few boulder problems and some top-rope options. The upper south face is a big dark slab with a bold, exposed feel and runouts on some lines, and its south exposure suits cold days while the west side stays shadier.

co_bootlegger_s_boulders.blurb: Bootlegger's Boulders is a cluster of large blocks in the Wet Mountains of southern Colorado, beside a highway west of Canon City and roughly forty minutes from Westcliffe. There is essentially no walk, since the boulders sit next to a big pull-off. Seventeen problems are recorded, mostly V0 to V3, with a few harder ones up to V5, though the pile holds many more blocks than that and likely more unlisted lines. It suits a relaxed afternoon of easy and moderate problems, with a few possible hard lines for strong climbers.

co_pharcyde_the.blurb: The Pharcyde is a secluded cliff band west of Monte Vista in the San Luis Valley, around 8,000 feet, among the newer areas developed near Penitente. Expect a half-mile uphill walk along a dirt road to reach it. The 17 climbs are mostly sport routes, with a few boulder problems, running from 5.10 up through the 5.13s, so it favors climbers working at harder grades. The rock is good quality, routes catch the morning sun, and the isolation means few other parties.

co_jazz_dome.blurb: Jazz Dome is a granite slab above the North Fork of the South Platte near Deckers, southwest of Denver, with the rock visible from the road and a short hike. It faces south and east, and cooler spring and fall days are the most comfortable. The 17 climbs mix sport, trad, top-rope and a couple of aid lines, mostly 5.6 to 5.11 with a bunch in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. Expect slabby, sometimes run-out climbing and a few loose spots, so route-finding and scoping lines in advance matter. It is quiet and low-key.

co_rattler_cliff_routes.blurb: Rattler Cliff is a secluded roadside crag near Del Norte in the San Luis Valley, at the head of a canyon around 8,300 feet. This section holds 17 sport and trad routes, mostly 5.10 and 5.11 with a few easier and a couple of 5.12 and 5.13 lines. Styles vary from pocketed prows and panels to a classic splitter crack. Shade makes spring through fall pleasant. Rock quality can be poor at the base and improves higher, so helmets are wise, and watch for rattlesnakes.
